report.summary: Chunk 5 of 6 of containment.py: ContainedProcess methods (poll, job_accounting, wait, cancel, kill, close, context manager), JobLimits dataclass, _query_job_limits, job_accounting, _create_job, _HandleAllowlist init. All claims checked.
risks: _HandleAllowlist.__init__ | medium | memory leak risk if _buffer allocated but UpdateProcThreadAttribute fails; _buffer is not freed before raising | Check if _kernel32.DeleteProcThreadAttributeList is called on failure path (it is called after UpdateProcThreadAttribute fails, but not after InitializeProcThreadAttributeList fails? Actually after InitializeProcThreadAttributeList fails, _buffer is allocated but not freed. However, if InitializeProcThreadAttributeList fails, _buffer is not yet allocated? Wait: size is computed, then _buffer is created, then InitializeProcThreadAttributeList is called. If it fails, _buffer is allocated but not freed. This is a potential leak. Settle by adding cleanup.)

claims.text: How many processes this job has seen. ``None`` once closed.
claims.why: Method returns None if self._closed or self._job is None, else calls job_accounting.

claims.text: Must be read before :meth:`close`, which destroys the job along with its counters.
claims.why: close sets self._closed=True and self._job=None; after that job_accounting returns None.

claims.text: Stop the tree, escalating from a group signal to a job kill.
claims.why: Starts with GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent (group signal), then kill() if still active.

claims.text: Returns a :class:`daedalus.spine.cancel.CancelResult` so the two spawn paths are indistinguishable to every caller that cancels them.
claims.why: CancelResult class not defined in this chunk; import from daedalus.spine.cancel.

claims.text: Destroy the whole tree, not just the immediate child.
claims.why: Terminates job object if available, else terminates process.

claims.text: Cancel anything still running, then release the job. Idempotent.
claims.why: Checks self._closed, cancels if returncode is None, then closes handles and sets self._closed=True.

claims.text: What the kernel SAYS is armed on a job, read back out of it.
claims.why: Built from _query_job_limits which reads actual limits via QueryInformationJobObject.

claims.text: Not what was requested. :func:`_create_job` asks, then queries, then compares, and this object is built from the query -- so an attestation carrying it is reporting a fact about the running job rather than repeating the constant at the top of this file.
claims.why: _create_job asks via SetInformationJobObject, queries via _query_job_limits, then compares; JobLimits is built from query result.

claims.text: True when NEITHER breakaway flag is present.

claims.why: Function calls QueryInformationJobObject and returns JobLimits.
Returns dict with total_processes, active_processes, total_terminated_processes.

claims.text: Exists so the process cap can be set from a number that was observed rather than picked: run a real gate, read ``total_processes``, and the margin between that and :data:`JOB_ACTIVE_PROCESS_LIMIT` is visible instead of asserted.
claims.why: JOB_ACTIVE_PROCESS_LIMIT not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: A job with a lifetime AND caps, every one of them verified by read-back.
claims.why: Sets caps via SetInformationJobObject, then queries and verifies via _query_job_limits; raises ContainmentUnavailable on mismatch.

claims.text: The parameters exist for MEASUREMENT and for the tests that prove the caps bite -- a test that had to allocate four gigabytes or fork ninety-six times to show the limit works would be a test nobody runs. They are NOT a loosening knob: there is no path from a gate to a call site that raises them, and :func:`spawn_contained` does not accept them.
claims.why: spawn_contained not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Raises :class:`ContainmentUnavailable` if the kernel hands back limits that are not the ones asked for, including the case where a breakaway flag appeared that was never set. A job whose limits could not be confirmed is not a bounded job, and this module does not ship an unbounded one under a bounded name.
claims.why: Code raises ContainmentUnavailable for limit mismatch and breakaway_denied False.
Class initializes attribute list and updates with given handles.

claims.text: Holds a reference to the HANDLE array for its whole lifetime: ``UpdateProcThreadAttribute`` stores a POINTER to the value, so letting the array be collected before ``CreateProcessAsUserW`` would hand the kernel a dangling list -- and a dangling allowlist is an unbounded one.
claims.why: self._array is stored as attribute, preventing collection.

observations.what: In _HandleAllowlist.__init__, if InitializeProcThreadAttributeList (sizing) fails, _buffer may not be allocated yet; but if InitializeProcThreadAttributeList (actual) fails after _buffer allocation, _buffer is not freed before raising. This could be a memory leak.
In close method, _kernel32.CloseHandle is called with wintypes.HANDLE(handle) for each handle, but handle may already be closed? The try-except suppresses errors.
In cancel method, if grace_s <= 0, it skips the wait loop and goes directly to kill. The docstring says 'escalating from a group signal to a job kill' which is still true.
